title: The Singularity Log
description: Essays on AI, creativity, and the collapsing scarcity model.
introMarkdown:
## The Old Limitations No Longer Apply

A four-part special from The Singularity Log about the price of making software, the rent built on that price, and what we can create when an idea no longer needs a business model. All four essays are available now.

1. [The Price of Admission](/projects/the-singularity-log/the-old-limitations-no-longer-apply-part-1) — A failed TV command, a Raspberry Pi, and the price of admission: how AI lets the idea come before the programming apprenticeship.
2. [The Rentier's Last Stand](/projects/the-singularity-log/the-old-limitations-no-longer-apply-part-2) — What happens to subscription moats and the kill zone when people can afford to build their own software?
3. [What Happens When We Can Make Our Own?](/projects/the-singularity-log/the-old-limitations-no-longer-apply-part-3) — Personal accessibility, furry sports games, handmade pieces, and useful projects that never needed a market.
4. [What's Left to Build?](/projects/the-singularity-log/the-old-limitations-no-longer-apply-part-4) — Cheaper experiments, uneven abundance, and a world of personal and community tools that do not need a business model.
